- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp drop, model tends to underestimate future price — correct by adding 1–2% to the forecast for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast shows a sharp rise, model overestimates — correct by subtracting 1–2% from the forecast for the next 3–5 days.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 70), model often overshoots in the following 5–7 days — reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast is trending downward, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates the true price by 1–3% when sentiment is positive — apply a +1% bias to the forecast for the first 10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.9 to -0.2), model often lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0% to account for sentiment shift.
